subject: Urgent: Arborwell private cluster — sustained p99 tail & 502 trend
messages:
From: Elliot Park <elliot.park@arborwell.io>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: maya.singh@arborwell.io
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service degradation this AM — p99 and 502 increase

Jonas / Laura —

We started seeing elevated p99s on our on-prem inference cluster around 08:30 local today and a correlated uptick in 502s for a subset of shorter inference requests (average token count ~60). Overall throughput is down ~18% from baseline and our internal SLAs are being missed. Attached is a trimmed bundle with logs and a K/V cache snapshot (support_log_20260518.tar.gz, kvcache_snapshot_0518.json).

What we've observed: 
- p50 unchanged, p90 +10%, p99 +55% (steady), 502s concentrated on a small set of backends serving model variant rwd-3b-quant
- Traffic hasn't increased. No code push on our side. 

We need immediate help to stabilize. Can Redwood run an emergency tuning pass (kernel selection, batching profile, and warmup policy) and propose a short-term fallback (alternate model variant or routing override)? We'd like an exec-level sync with your CTO / head of ops if this looks multi-hour.

Thanks,
Elliot
Elliot Park
SRE Lead, Arborwell Health
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Elliot Park <elliot.park@arborwell.io>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@arborwell.io>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 17:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service degradation this AM — p99 and 502 increase

Elliot —

Thanks for the data. I've kicked off a priority investigation with our Private runtime SREs and asked Karthik to pre-check kernel selection heuristics for the rwd-3b-quant variant. Quick notes from initial triage: 
- Early signal looks like KV cache churn + decoder kernel mismatch under the current batching policy for short requests. That would explain stable p50 but widened tail.
- 502s likely coming from decode timeouts at the runtime layer when a request misses the warm cache and gets pushed into a longer execution path.

Immediate next steps (we'll act in parallel):
1) Marissa will run a conservative routing override to move ~25% of traffic to rwd-3b-fp16 on safe nodes for 1h to relieve pressure.
2) Karthik will adjust continuous batching threshold: reduce max-batch-wait from 12ms -> 6ms for short-request routes to keep per-request latency bounded.
3) We'll provision a short warmup job for the hot prefix set to rebuild KV entries.
4) Requesting Arborwell SREs to provide a stable sample keyset and confirm any recent config drift.

If any of this looks risky, call it out now. We aim to have a mitigation live within 30-45m. If we can't bring p99 down by 60% in that window we'll escalate to exec sync.

Jonas Weber
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Elliot Park <elliot.park@arborwell.io>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 18:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service degradation this AM — p99 and 502 increase

Elliot —

I've applied a routing override on your staging nodes and will incrementally apply to a quarter of prod paths in 10-minute steps. I'll post metrics as we go. Notes on the change:
- Traffic split: 75% rwd-3b-quant (baseline), 25% rwd-3b-fp16 (fall-back)
- No config reload required; using runtime routing rules so rollback is instant.

Attaching the initial rollout graph. If you see any regression revert will be immediate.

- Marissa
Attachment: rollout_split_20260518.png (image)
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@arborwell.io>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Elliot Park <elliot.park@arborwell.io>, kai.morgan@srepartner.io
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 18:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service degradation this AM — p99 and 502 increase

Thanks Marissa — we've observed p99 drop ~18% after the first step and 502 rate halved. Good progress.

Couple asks from our side: 
- Can you share the exact batching/timeout delta applied so we can mirror locally?
- We're planning to open an on-call incident (INC-AR-221) and would like Redwood to add a short remediation runbook entry we can keep with our incident notes.

Also, Kai from our third-party SRE partner will join the loop for root cause continuity.

Maya
Maya Singh
VP Engineering, Arborwell Health
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@arborwell.io>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 19:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service degradation this AM — Service tuning details and follow-up

Maya / team —

Two technical notes and the exact changes I pushed: 
- Batching: reduced max_batch_wait_ms from 12 -> 6 for the short-request routing key; also lowered batch_pack_min_tokens to 8 to avoid over-packing small requests.
- Timeouts: increased decode pipeline soft-timeout from 850ms -> 1100ms at the runtime layer to avoid early 502s while KV warms; we'll roll this back after stable warm cache.
- Kernel Selection: forced runtime to prefer the alternate decoder kernel (decoder_v2_fastpath) for the rwd-3b-quant variant on the affected node pool. This kernel has higher p50 but much better p99 under KV churn.

I also kicked off a controlled KV-prefetch job targeting the top 120 prefixes observed in your logs — should complete in ~25m.

I'll follow up with a short runbook blurb you can paste into INC-AR-221. If you'd like, we can create a permanent playbook entry in your Confluence space.

- Karthik
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@arborwell.io>, Elliot Park <elliot.park@arborwell.io>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kai.morgan@srepartner.io
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service degradation this AM — stabilization and exec next steps

Maya / Elliot / Kai —

Glad to see the immediate mitigation reduced tail latency and 502s. A couple of items I want to capture and propose for executive visibility: 
- Short-term (we have actioned): routing override, batching/timeouts adjustment, KV-prefetch complete.
- Medium-term (next 72h): run a kernel A/B on non-peak windows to validate decoder_v2_fastpath stability across your traffic mix; update deployment quantization profile to reduce warm misses; add an automated warmup job post-deploy.
- Risk: if your production traffic shifts to a much higher proportion of tiny requests, the fallback FP16 variant will increase cost and memory; we should model cost impact before permanent routing change.

Request: please let me know whether Arborwell wants a 30-min exec-level call today between your CTO and our Head of Eng (or me) to briefly align on SLA mitigation and a 72h action plan. If you prefer, we can keep this at the SRE/ops level.

I'll also attach the post-mortem stub and our recommended remediation timeline to this thread by EOD.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
